To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified a new regulatory CD8+CD4+Foxp3 T cell population in colorectal tumour tissue, which is able to suppress the proliferation of CD4+CD4− T cells and to inhibit the production of Th1 cytokines by conventional T cells ex vivo, suggesting a role in tumoral immune escape.
we identified a new regulatory CD8+Fox3+ T cell population in colorectal tumour tissue and that these CD8+ regulatory T cells have strong immunosupressive properties in vitro.
we identified a novel regulatory T cell population in colorectal cancer that has strong immunosuppresive properties and that may contribute to tumour immune escape.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of a new population of regulatory CD8+CD4+ T cells in colorectual cancer tissue.
the identification of a new regulatory T-cell population in colorectal tumour tissue and with the characterization of their suppressive properties.
the role of regulatory T cells in colorectral cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of CD8+ regulatory T cells in the tumor microenvironment of CRC may contribute to the immunosuppression observed in this disease.
T8reg cells are present in the blood and in the tissue of CRC patients and are associated with a more advanced disease.
the presence of CD8+FoxP3+ T cells in CRC tissue is a marker of poor prognosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a new population of regulatory T cells (CD8+CD25+) in colorectal cancer (CD8+Treg), which are increased in number in tumour tissue compared to normal colonic tissue.
CD8+CD28− T cells are the major source of CD8+FoxP3+ T cells and that CD8+Fox3+ T cells are able to inhibit CD4+ T cell proliferation in a dose-dependent fashion.
we have identified CD8+ regulatory T cells in colorectral cancer tissue and that they have immunosuppressive capacity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we found a significant increase in CD8+CD4+Foxp3+, CD8+CD45RO+Foxp3-, and CD8+CD62L+Foxp3- T cells in the peripheral blood of CRC patients compared to controls, and that the number of CD8+FoxP3+ T cells in the blood of CRC patients correlates with the stage of the tumour.
the immune response to CRC is not only mediated by CD4+ T cells, but also involves a CD8+ regulatory T cell population.
CD8+FoxP3+ T cells are present in the tumor microenvironment and may contribute to immune escape.
